mission_04: Outstanding! You have modeled in-memory computing using memristor crossbar arrays. Your implementation demonstrates the fundamental principle: matrix-vector multiplication is performed in a single analog step through Ohm's law (I = V * G) and Kirchhoff's law (current summation). The differential crossbar pair handles signed weights by separating positive and negative conductances. Device noise simulation shows the practical challenges of analog computing — conductance variability introduces computation errors that must be managed through calibration and error correction. In-memory computing promises orders of magnitude improvement in energy efficiency for AI workloads by eliminating data movement, the dominant energy cost in traditional architectures.
